name: Remove Large File from History
problem: Someone accidentally committed a 500MB video file or database dump a month ago. Even though you deleted it in a later commit, the `.git` folder is still massive because Git remembers the file's history forever.

steps.title: Use git filter-repo (Recommended)
steps.description: Git's native `filter-branch` is deprecated because it's slow and error-prone. The official recommendation is the third-party `git filter-repo` tool (requires Python).
steps.code:
# 1. Install git-filter-repo (e.g., pip install git-filter-repo, or brew install git-filter-repo)

# 2. Analyze what's taking up space
git filter-repo --analyze

# 3. Look at .git/filter-repo/analysis/path-all-sizes.txt to find the file

# 4. Strip the file from all history
git filter-repo --path "path/to/massive-file.mp4" --invert-paths

steps.title: Force push the rewritten history
steps.description: Because you rewrote the repository's history from the ground up, all commit hashes have changed. You must force push to the remote.
steps.code:
git push origin --force --all
git push origin --force --tags

steps.title: Tell your team to re-clone
steps.description: Anyone who pulls the repo now will get horrible merge conflicts. They should delete their local copy and clone fresh from the server.
steps.code:
# Teammates should run:
rm -rf the-project
git clone https://github.com/team/the-project.git

alternatives.title: Using BFG Repo-Cleaner
alternatives.description: Another excellent, fast alternative to filter-repo. Requires Java.
alternatives.code:
# 1. Download bfg.jar
# 2. Run it against your repo
java -jar bfg.jar --delete-files massive-file.mp4 my-repo.git

# 3. Clean up the git database
cd my-repo.git
git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now --aggressive

# 4. Force push
git push origin --force
